In this analysis we explore whether body mass and flipper length differ across the three penguin species: Adelie, Chinstrap, and Gentoo.
Data: Palmer Penguins, Palmer Station Antarctica LTER. Available under a CC0 license.

library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)

title: Penguin Body Size by Species
text:
Preparing the data
We first load the dataset and remove rows with missing values.

penguins_clean <- penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g), !is.na(flipper_length_mm), !is.na(species))

title: Penguin Body Size by Species
text:
Summary statistics by species
We compute the mean and standard deviation of body mass and flipper length for each species.

penguins_summary <- penguins_clean |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarize(
    mean_body_mass = mean(body_mass_g),
    sd_body_mass = sd(body_mass_g),
    mean_flipper_length = mean(flipper_length_mm),
    n = n()
  )

From this table, we can see that Gentoo penguins are noticeably heavier than the other two species.

title: Penguin Body Size by Species
text:
Conclusion
Based on the table and figure above, Gentoo penguins are clearly heavier than the other two species, while Adelie and Chinstrap have more similar body mass distributions.

title: Penguin Bill Shape by Island
text:
Conclusion
Bill length and depth differ across islands mainly because each island is dominated by a different species. Biscoe is home mostly to Gentoo and Adelie penguins, while Dream has a mix of Adelie and Chinstrap, and Torgersen has only Adelie penguins. This explains the differences we see in the summary statistics above.
